meta.title: i-MaCHeL: a cluster randomised trial of a preschool healthy-lifestyle programme

question.text: The general aim of this study is to evaluate the efficacy of the 3-month i-MaCHeL programme, a web-based, theory-driven intervention, in changing weight-related behaviour in preschool child-parent dyads in Terengganu, Malaysia.
question.tertium_comparationis: the between-group difference in BMI z-score change from baseline at 3 and 9 months
question.scope: 460 child-parent dyads from 12 preschools in Kuala Terengganu and Kuala Nerus, Terengganu, Malaysia; children aged 5 and 6; 3-month intervention, outcomes at 3 and 9 months post-baseline.
question.completion_criterion: The question is answered when the between-group difference in BMI z-score change is estimated with a cluster-adjusted repeated-measures model and reported with its confidence interval.

method.approach: Single-blind, two-group cluster randomised controlled trial; general linear model repeated measures with ANCOVA and intention-to-treat analysis.
sources: 460 child-parent dyads recruited from 12 preschools in Kuala Terengganu and Kuala Nerus
Anthropometric measurements, three-day food records and validated questionnaires collected at baseline, 3 and 9 months
method.procedure: Randomise 12 preschools 1:1 in six blocks; deliver 13 weekly online modules and teacher-led classroom sessions to the intervention arm; give the control arm general health newsletters; measure BMI z-score, diet, activity, screen time, quality of life and parental measures; analyse with repeated-measures ANCOVA adjusted for clustering, baseline values and covariates; impute missing data.
validity_conditions: Randomisation is performed by an independent researcher at preschool level
The primary analysis adjusts for the clustering effect and baseline outcome values
Intention-to-treat is applied to all randomised dyads

results.claim: The combination of classroom activities and the interactive web-based programme sustains child-parent engagement and changes weight-related behaviour more than the active control.
results.falsifier: The between-group difference in BMI z-score change is indistinguishable from zero at 3 and 9 months after adjustment for clustering and baseline values.
results.evidence_needed: Anthropometric measurements and questionnaire outcomes for both arms at baseline, 3 and 9 months.

warrant.gap_statement: Most preschool-based trials of weight-related behaviour change were conducted in high-income countries, and no study integrates classroom activities with a web-based programme for child-parent dyads in Malaysia.
evidence: Adab et al., WAVES cluster randomised trial, BMJ, 2018
Rashid et al., i-MaCHeL protocol, PLOS ONE, 2022
Malaysian Dietary Guidelines for Children and Adolescents, 2013
